what_happened: The agent running Athena told Sri that the planner-escalation job had landed and was fine. It based this on the monitor's "landed" line and the verifier summary, and did not read the drain log after the landing. The landing added new planner_revision_* keys to athena.toml. The drain was still running the older build, which refused those keys. Readings failed for about 5 minutes, until a routine drain restart at 22:07 UTC. An independent review found the problem. No job work was judged bad.
cause: The agent reports on shared state without checking what the state actually is, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was the health of the running drain after a landing. A "landed" line and a verifier summary say the job's change merged. They say nothing about whether the live drain still works with the new config. Athena does not tie a "fine" claim to a post-landing check of the drain log. The only guard is the agent's own habit of reading the records first.
other_causes: A job that adds a config field lands while the running drain is an older build that rejects it. That is the same shape as the self-landing config-field class, and no pre-landing warning or automatic drain restart covers it.
The drain's restart after a config-changing landing is routine and manual, so there is a window where the live build and the config disagree.
open_hypotheses: Whether the drain log showed the refusal clearly at the time, so that reading it would have caught the problem within seconds.
Whether the planner-escalation job's own checks could have flagged that the installed build rejects the new keys.
contradictions: The earlier cases in this class are about misreading a job's or item's identity or status. This case is about reporting a landing as fine without reading the drain log, so the match is by shared cause only.
prevention: Add a post-landing check that runs after any landing which changes athena.toml. It would load the new config with the running drain's build and scan the drain log for errors, then report "landed and drain healthy" or "landed, drain refusing config" in the same line the monitor prints. Until then, the agent should not call a config-changing landing fine without reading the drain output that follows it.
proposed_request: Add a post-landing health check to Athena. After any landing that changes athena.toml, load the landed config with the running drain's build and read the drain log lines written after the landing. The outcome is that the monitor's "landed" line also says whether the drain accepted the config, and flags a refusal, such as an unknown key, right away. Acceptance: (1) a test with a config key the running build does not know shows the landing line flagged as drain-refusing; (2) a landing with a known config shows it marked healthy; (3) a landing that does not touch athena.toml is unchanged; (4) add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
